sentences.text:
For the Petitioner(s) : Mr. Vishnu Prabhakar Pathak, Advocate Ms. Apurva, Advocate, For the State :
Mr. Lily Sahay, App Mr. Abhay Shankar Dayal, Advocate Mr. Anurag Kashyap, Advocate
-----
02/ 10.07.2025 Heard the parties.

2. This anticipatory bail application under Sections 482 & 484 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha
Sanhita (Bnss), 2023, has been preferred by the petitioner apprehending his arrest for offences
under Sections 419/420/467/468/471/120(B) of the Ipc and 66(B)/66(C)/66(D) of It Act.
3.  Learned A.P.P. representing the State and learned counsel for the informant opposes the prayer for anticipatory bail.

4. After going through the record, I find that the only material against the petitioner is there is confessional statement of the co-accused to the effect that he was operating the entire bank accounts.
5. The learned APP submits that there is no transfer of any amount in the account of this petitioner from any source or from the account of any beneficiary or other persons.

sentences.text: Since, there is no supporting evidence of transfer of money in the account of this petitioner from any beneficiaries, the only stand-alone evidence against the petitioner is the confessional statement of the co-accused.
7. Considering the aforesaid facts, I am inclined to allow this application.
8. Accordingly, this Anticipatory Bail Application stands 2025:JHHC:18597 allowed.

The petitioner,
above named, is directed to surrender before the learned court below within four weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order and on the event of his surrender or arrest, he shall be released on bail on furnishing bail bonds of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand), with two sureties of the like amount each, to the satisfaction of learned AJC-II-cum-Special Judge Cyber Crimes, Ranchi in connection with Cyber P.S. Case No.03/2023, subject to the condition that one of the bailers should be a close relative of the petitioner and he should be a resident of State of Jharkhand, having sufficient landed property in his name or in the name of his ancestors in which they are having share and to that effect, he has to file an affidavit before the Trial Court indicating his share in the property.

( ANANDA SEN, J.) Sandeep. Cp-3 Ranjan Kumar Dutta vs The State Of Jharkhand on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3204232/
